newsitem.title: USA: Phila. takes steps toward tax lien sale -- paper.
newsitem.headline: Phila. takes steps toward tax lien sale -- paper.

text.p: Philadelphia is taking the first steps toward selling delinquent tax liens, notifying taxpayers to pay now or face a much tougher collection agency down the road, the Philadelphia Inquirer reported Friday.

Residents late on their real estate tax payments are being told they have 14 days to contact the city and commit to a payment plan. After that, property owners may have to pay legal fees on top of their overdue taxes.

Then, probably by the end of June, the city plans to get out of the delinquent tax collection business entirely, selling off the liens to a private company that will pursue the cases instead of the city.

About 90,000 properties are involved in the sale, and the city is hoping to get about 80 cents on the dollar when the liens are sold. Acting as its own collection agency, the city normally expects to collect just 44 cents on the dollar.
Based on the city's projections, a portfolio of liens worth $173 million would net $138 million for the city and its school district, which would take 55 percent of the total under the plan.
City council still must take a final vote to approve the deal when bids for the liens are received. PaineWebber Inc. is the city's senior manager on the deal.
